name: Erkin Wendt-Frempong
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
description:
Erkin Wendt-Frempong are tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 40, there's something unfinished about their face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and they make no effort to hide it.

They arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and have been working off both ever since. They work as a ghost out of Dockside, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

they are not the most talented ghost in Meridian 88, but they might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality
Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
blind_spots: Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
psychology.secret: Erkin Wendt-Frempong can't read. Hides it behind voice interfaces and memorization. The shame is older than the chrome.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Flat affect, monotone delivery. The content is terrifying but the voice never rises.
speech_patterns.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' — either royal or dissociative, nobody asks
example_lines: "Clean means no witnesses, no evidence, no questions. That's three things. I charge for each."
"The target will stop breathing at the specified time. What you do with that information is your concern."

story_hooks: A corporate black site Erkin Wendt-Frempong once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know their face
Erkin Wendt-Frempong intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
A crew member from Erkin Wendt-Frempong's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
narrative_function: Erkin Wendt-Frempong is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When they make a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of their stories.
augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs
daily_life: Irregular schedule dictated by contract timing. Between jobs: equipment maintenance, physical training, and the careful management of a reputation that exists entirely through word of mouth. Drinks at establishments where runners gather — not for pleasure, but for market intelligence.

weaknesses: trust issues that limit crew effectiveness
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
habits: Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
breaking_points: Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Betrayal by the one person they actually trust — the single point of failure in their emotional architecture
